plan.title: Verstappen Wins a Chaotic 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix
plan.description: Max Verstappen won the 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix after a frantic race on the Nevada streets. Here is how Mercedes lost the lead, McLaren took the podium and Ferrari collided.

beats.narration: Two Mercedes cars fought for the lead all race long, and then both fell off the podium in the final laps. Here is how the Las Vegas Grand Prix turned upside down.

beats.narration: Max Verstappen won. The four-time World Champion held off a race-long challenge to take his third victory on the streets of Nevada, finishing the 50 laps in one hour, twenty-seven minutes and thirty-nine seconds.
It was a frantic race, with karting-style passes for the lead. Verstappen kept a calm head, outdriving and out-strategising both Mercedes drivers, for his fourth win in six races.

props.text: Karting-style passes for the lead, and a calm head won it.

beats.narration: The Mercedes pair led the fight for most of the race. Then George Russell hit the wall, and Kimi Antonelli dropped back late. That let McLaren take second and third.
Lando Norris finished second, just 0.639 seconds behind the winner. Oscar Piastri took third, 1.529 seconds back. Kimi Antonelli was fourth, only 2.574 seconds off the lead.
Pierre Gasly took fifth, managing cooling problems on his Alpine. Team mate Franco Colapinto was sixth, so Alpine had two cars well inside the points.
Ferrari had an eventful afternoon. Lewis Hamilton took a ten-second penalty for leaving the track and gaining an advantage against Norris. Later he made contact with team mate Charles Leclerc.
Hamilton finished seventh. Carlos Sainz scored valuable points for Williams in eighth. Russell recovered to ninth, and Leclerc rounded out the top ten.
Antonelli lost out on the result, but not on pace. He was the most threatening for the win he has looked so far, and he showed he is a proper contender on street circuits.

props.text: A loser from the result, but certainly not in performance.

beats.narration: So the lesson from Las Vegas: the fastest car does not always win. Verstappen stayed calm while Mercedes faded, and McLaren collected the podium behind him.
